 Vlogger Norman Mangusin arrested anew
 Karen De Guzman ,
 ABS-CBN News
 Published November 19, 2026 08:07 PM PHT 
 MANILA — Vlogger Norman Mangusin, who goes by the alias “Francis Leo Marcos,” was arrested anew on Thursday over the alleged illegal use of a police uniform, the National Police Commission (NAPOLCOM) said.
 In an interview, NAPOLCOM Vice Chairperson and Executive Officer Rafael Vicente Calinisan said operatives of the police’s Criminal Investigation and Detection Group-Detective and Special Operations Unit (CIDG-DSOU) arrested Mangusin after serving a warrant of arrest.
 “Mangusin is now in police custody and as we speak, is being transported to Camp Crame after the service of the warrant of arrest for the offense of illegal use of uniforms,” Calinisan said. 
 The warrant was issued by the Quezon City Regional Trial Court Branch 224 for alleged violation of Article 179 of the Revised Penal Code, or the illegal use of uniforms or insignia, in relation to Republic Act No. 10175, or the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 According to Calinisan, the warrant indicates that bail is not necessary unless required by the court.
 The arrest stemmed from a viral photograph of Mangusin wearing a ceremonial blue police uniform, which prompted an investigation by the Philippine National Police and NAPOLCOM in February.
 PNP, Napolcom probe vlogger for wearing police uniform in viral photo Authorities said the use of a police uniform or insignia by someone who is not authorized to wear it could constitute a violation of the law.
 This is Mangusin's third arrest this year.
 He was first arrested  in February over 12 counts of unjust vexation stemming from a complaint filed by fellow vlogger Mark Jayson Warnakulahewa. 
 ADVERTISEMENT
 He was released on February 28 after posting P120,000 bail.
 He was arrested again in October over three counts of cyberlibel filed by the wife of Warnakulahewa.
 The charges stemmed from alleged defamatory online posts. 
 Mangusin has yet to issue a statement on his latest arrest.
